question: Ramesh invested ₹1,232 at 5% p.a. simple interest in a bank. What amount will he get after 3 years?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Total Interest %** = Rate × Time = 5% × 3 = 15%.

**Total Amount %** = 100% (Principal) + 15% (Interest) = 115%.

**Amount** = 1232 × 1.15 = ₹1416.80.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1416.80.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** **Principal (P)** = ₹1232, **Rate (R)** = 5%, **Time (T)** = 3 years.

**Formula Used:** Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100; Amount (A) = P + SI

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4649271ad985d3793d5c2c83d7809be6aeb645c6fc2282d6c2458a33513e0d37.png] 

⇒ SI = (1232 × 5 × 3) ÷ 100

⇒ SI = (1232 × 15) ÷ 100

⇒ SI = 18480 ÷ 100 = ₹184.80

⇒ Amount = Principal + Simple Interest

⇒ Amount = 1232 + 184.80 = ₹1416.80

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1416.80.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Simple Interest vs Compound Interest

Simple Interest is calculated only on the **Principal** amount, whereas Compound Interest is calculated on the **Principal plus accumulated interest**.

Rate of Interest (R)

If the rate is given **per annum**, the time must be converted to **years**. R = (SI × 100) ÷ (P × T).

Amount Formula

The total **Maturity Value** or **Amount** is given by A = P(1 + RT/100).
